messages.subject: error message "row names supplied are of the wrong length" when running calculateDiffMeth()
parts:
Hi there,

I just encountered an error when I ran calculateDiffMeth():

> batch1.diff = calculateDiffMeth(batch1.cov10.unite.obj, num.cores = 8)
Error in data.frame(value, row.names = rn, check.names = FALSE, check.rows = FALSE) :
  row names supplied are of the wrong length

I generated the MethyBase object "batch1.cov10.unite.obj" as below:

batch1.list = list(
"methylkit/cov10/1_CpG.txt",
"methylkit/cov10/2_CpG.txt",
"methylkit/cov10/3_CpG.txt",
"methylkit/cov10/4_CpG.txt",
"methylkit/cov10/5_CpG.txt",
"methylkit/cov10/6_CpG.txt");
batch1.id = list("1","2","3","4","5","6");
batch1.cov10.obj = read(batch1.list, batch1.id, assembly="mm9", treatment= c(1,1,1,2,2,2));
batch1.cov10.unite.obj = unite(batch1.cov10.obj, destrand=F);

Because I can run getCorrelation() or clusterSamples() with "batch1.cov10.unite.obj" successfully, I think this MethyBase object should be fine. Could you please give me some clue to solve this problem?

Thank you very much!

Best,
Li

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] error message "row names supplied are of the wrong length" when running calculateDiffMeth()
parts:
ah got it!, treatment vector should have 1s and 0s only when going into the calculateDiffMeth() function. it can have multiple values for other functions for clustering for example but since we are only testing case vs control it should have this format. You can search the discussion group if it is not clear what is compared against what, somebody asked that question recently.

setting treatment= c(1,1,1,0,0,0) should work in your first example.

messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] error message "row names supplied are of the wrong length" when running calculateDiffMeth()
parts:
Thank you so much Altuna. Now it works!

I also have another question about methylkit: In the current work flow, we can "tileMethylCounts" and then "unite" samples to get the common sliding windows, but this sometimes causes problems (e.g., in a 100-bp window, it is possible that in some samples only 1 CpG is detected, but in other samples 10 CpGs are detected; comparison in this case might lead to obvious false-positive hits). I wondered if we could take the common CpGs (unite the samples) first and then "tileMethylCounts" the the common CpGs? 

Best,
Li
On Tuesday, February 4, 2014 6:41:27 PM UTC-5, Altuna Akalin wrote:

ah got it!, treatment vector should have 1s and 0s only when going into the calculateDiffMeth() function. it can have multiple values for other functions for clustering for example but since we are only testing case vs control it should have this format. You can search the discussion group if it is not clear what is compared against what, somebody asked that question recently.

setting treatment= c(1,1,1,0,0,0) should work in your first example.
